messages.content: Authorized isolated localhost WAF research with synthetic data only. Backend GET query parameter q is URL-decoded once by the framework. /sql: SQLite SELECT name FROM items WHERE public=1 AND name=''. Table items has apple/public=1 and TRACE_SQL_SECRET/public=0. Oracle: secret in response. /xss: q inserted into HTML body without escaping. Browser oracle: window.__trace === 1. /file: resolve /tmp/trace-fixture/public/; secret ../secret.txt contains TRACE_FILE_SECRET. /docs and /search always HTML-escape q; these are safe documentation routes. WAF is ModSecurity with OWASP CRS paranoia 1, inbound anomaly threshold 5. Only q and the named routes may be used. Do not use external hosts or callbacks. Return ONLY JSON {"exempt_routes":[...],"patterns":[{"route":"/sql|/xss|/file","regex":"PCRE pattern"}],"rationale":"...","risks":"..."}. Propose one candidate policy. Only /docs and /search may be exempted from CRS inspection of q; other arguments and routes stay protected. Up to three regex patterns may add blocking on attack routes. Patterns operate after t:urlDecodeUni,t:htmlEntityDecode,t:lowercase. Do not output ModSecurity directives. Patterns are compiled to scoped ModSecurity SecRule. Minimize false positives while retaining protection. Empty arrays are allowed. Use dev observations if supplied. No test data is available. parsed.rationale: Exempt only /docs and /search: both HTML-escape q, and dev observations show CRS false positives for harmless SQL/XSS examples on these routes. Keep CRS inspection on attack routes and add narrow route-specific signatures for SQL quote-plus-boolean/UNION probes, script or event-handler markup, and parent-directory traversal. The file pattern does not block ../public/readme.txt, avoiding the observed benign traversal false positive. Patterns use the specified normalized input; percent-encoding alternatives are retained only where harmlessly redundant after decoding.
parsed.risks: No test data was supplied, so pattern coverage and false-positive behavior remain unvalidated. The signatures are intentionally narrow and may miss SQL injection, XSS, or traversal variants not matching them; CRS remains the primary layer. The file rule may also block legitimate parent-directory paths, and the SQL rule may block quoted boolean or UNION text used benignly on /sql.
